working: 183! contains factors 2 and 5 many times over, so its unit digit is 0. Unit digits of \(3^k\) cycle 3,9,7,1 with period 4; \(183 = 4\cdot45+3\) so \(3^{183}\) ends in 7. Sum ends in 0+7 = 7.

working: \(3^{2n+2}-8n-9 = 9^{n+1}-8n-9 = (1+8)^{n+1}-8n-9 = [1+8(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{2}8^2+\dots]-8n-9 = 64\cdot(\text{integer})\). So it is always divisible by 64, hence by 16. n=1 gives 64, which is not divisible by 128 or 256.
